name: Pyritinol
summary: Pyritinol also called pyridoxine disulfide or pyrithioxine (European drug names Encephabol, Encefabol, Cerbon 6) is a semi-synthetic water-soluble analog of vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine HCl). It was produced in 1961 by Merck Laboratories by bonding 2 vitamin B6 compounds (pyridoxine) together with a disulfide bridge.

uses.text: Since the early 1990s it has been sold as a nootropic dietary supplement in the United States.

sideEffects.text: Adverse effects include nausea, headache, and rarely allergic reaction (mild skin reactions). A 2004 survey of six case reports suggested a link between pyritinol and severe cholestatic hepatitis when on several drugs for certain diseases.

pharmacology.en: Studies suggest it increases the brain's use of glucose and may boost the release of acetylcholine, but how it works is not well understood. It does not act as vitamin B6 in the body.
pharmacology.zh: 研究顯示它可能增加大腦對葡萄糖的利用，並可能促進乙醯膽鹼釋放，但作用方式仍不清楚。它在體內並不會發揮維生素 B6 的作用。
pharmacology.zhHans: 研究显示它可能增加大脑对葡萄糖的利用，并可能促进乙酰胆碱释放，但作用方式仍不清楚。它在体内并不会发挥维生素 B6 的作用。

fact.en: Pyritinol is two vitamin B6 molecules joined by a disulfide bridge, a pair of linked sulfur atoms. It was developed by Merck in Germany.
fact.zh: 吡硫醇是兩個維生素 B6 分子以雙硫橋（兩個相連的硫原子）連在一起，由德國默克公司開發。
fact.zhHans: 吡硫醇是两个维生素 B6 分子以双硫桥（两个相连的硫原子）连在一起，由德国默克公司开发。
